text: Please accept your shoes at the door.
why: Nonsense either way: neither 'accept' nor 'except your shoes' means 'take off/leave'. The pair is also reversed (marked incorrect, 'corrected' to except). Note is wrong.

text: We accepted the last question on the exam.
why: Reversed pair: the text is correct English. 'excepted the last question' is a rare formal verb and not what learners need; the note 'Except = not including' doesn't fit a verb.

text: The old bridge is not passable in winter.
why: Marked incorrect, but the text is correct and the correction is identical to it.

text: It is imposible to finish this today.
why: The mistake is single s (imposible) and has nothing to do with -able/-ible. The rule-related error would be 'impossable'.
correct_word tests ss, not the -able/-ible ending. Use 'impossable' instead.

text: Choose the correct spelling: It is ___ to learn a language in one day.
why: The only distractor, 'imposible', differs in ss, not in the ending, so it doesn't test the rule. Use 'impossable'.

text: They accepted the smallest room from the list.
why: Reversed pair: the text is correct English. 'excepted the smallest room from the list' is a rare formal verb, so the 'correction' teaches a wrong pattern.

text: The school does not accept late students.
why: Reversed pair: the text is correct. 'does not except late students' is wrong, and the note 'Except = not including' doesn't fit a verb.

text: Choose the correct spelling: The label was easy to read and ___.
why: Tautological sentence ('easy to read and readable'), so it is poor model English.

text: The company accepted this item from the delivery.
why: Reversed pair: the text is correct English. 'excepted this item from the delivery' is an odd, rare verb use, presented as the correct form.

text: The schedule is not changeable after Friday.
why: Marked incorrect, but the text is correct and the correction is identical to it.

text: The office is closed ___ Wednesday afternoon.
why: The natural word is 'on' ('closed on Wednesday afternoon'). With 'except' the meaning is odd: it says the office is only open on Wednesday afternoon.

text: Choose the word: The school does not ___ mobile phones in class.
why: Unnatural sense: we say 'allow' phones in class, not 'accept'. It teaches accept = allow.

text: Choose the correct spelling: The date is ___ in the settings.
why: The only distractor, 'changeible', is a form nobody writes, so the task is trivial. The real learner error is 'changable'.
